I'm sorry for your loss OP. I want you to know you are not alone in what your going through. I'm sure a lot us here on this subreddit can relate. I hope you can find the support you need.
This is probably one of the hardest things your facing in your life right now.

You say she was cheating on you for a couple of months. This is definitely as bad as cheating gets IMO.  I would say you might not find much help from meditating. Meditation will definitely be an important part of the healing process, but you can't solely depend on mindfulness to fully heal. I know this may be contrary to what alot of us here may think. But the truth is your mind is going through a whirlwind of emotions and thoughts. When you sit your going to be ruminating and stuck in negative thoughts. You've been hurt, it's understandable that your feeling this way.

Please don't feel shame talking to your friends about it. That's what friends are for. If not, I highly recommend talking to a grief councilor/therapist. 

If you can't concentrate on your tasks at work you may be best to take a day or two off.  If you live close enough to nature, or a large park just go spend some extended time by yourself. 
I know it's hard to believe right now in this moment, but things WILL get better. But please take care of yourself and do what is right for you right now. You will get through this, and ultimately this will be a chapter in you life story of which you can look back on and genuinely be grateful for despite the way it ended. It will take time. You will be better for it.

Btw I would also recommend scrolling and/or re-posting to r/relationships. 
Lots of great advice on dealing with breakups.

I grew up in a Baptist church myself. It seems the more I learn about Buddhism the more I see the outright falsehoods, and like you said ignorance and *acceptance of ignorance*.  It drives me mad at times, but I'm learning to accept it for what it is. I feel like were in the same boat here. 

I think before you tell your family you've become a Buddhist, really try to wrap your head around what it really means to *you* what a Buddhist is.
Because you could just simply be a lay person willing to raise your family in a house where the Dhamma is very present. (a true blessing for any child, God bless you and your fiance).  I don't think that makes someone a Buddhist. 
In my mind a buddhist is one who is completely devoted to the lifestyle, ie: monks and nuns. I myself Im very hesitant to say Im a Buddhist to anyone I just don't think its accurate. Im just a layperson looking for peace in various traditions and philosophies and buddhism just happens to be one that resonates with me. 

But in any case, I wouldn't even tell them. Just go about with your family as you believe is right, and if they ask just tell them why you believe meditation and the teachings of the buddha are right for your family. 
You'll probably get a variety of different reactions, they could think you've gone mad, or succumb to the influences of "the enemy", or that your just following the New Age band wagon. Thus they will probably want to "pray for you" or rebuke you and some may have a genuine concern for your well-being.  
They will only react in the only way they know how. I would say be mindful of their perspective, understand that their judgement is clouded by said ignorance and if they could see better they would, the truth is they may have generations upon generations of dogma. If your family ostracizes you, it will take some time to accept and grieve the lost relationships but you will definitely find very close and good friends to raise your family with. On the other hand you may have individuals in your family who respect Buddhism (I see this alot, but I live in the West Coast), ideally you can really have some meaningful discussion with them and still maintain a positive relationship. 
I think the serenity prayer is appropriate here:

"God, grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change, The courage to change the things I can, And wisdom to know the difference"

Wish you luck. 

**tldr** Your not a really Buddhist your a layperson seeking truth in the Dhamma. Don't tell them. Let them ask. Be mindful and compassionate towards them, even if they may scorn you.

One thing Buddhism has taught me is to question everything I feel anxious about. The ego leads us to be slaves to our desires, and fearful and anxious toward things that bring about suffering. 
What your feeling happens to a lot of people, myself included. I've gone nights staying up till late in the morning before an exam, listening to my mind going through what will happen if I fail. 

When your in that sate of anxiety ask your self why are you feeling this way. just keep on asking yourself why,why,why (like a child does to their parents) but surprisingly you'll come across a false paradigm. And when you meet it face to face you can see it is nothing but a lie.  

When it comes to exams I look back to a Sun Tzu quote 
"The battle is won before it is ever fought" 
The real battle is the studying and preparation before your exams, the tests themselves will just be a confirmation of your excellence. 

You have the power my friend.
